steps.title: Definition
steps.body: A warm up is a period of light exercise that prepares the body for more strenuous activity. It gradually increases heart rate, body temperature and blood flow to working muscles.

steps.title: Exam Tip
steps.body: Dynamic stretching is recommended for warm ups. Static stretching is more appropriate for cool downs. Make sure you know the difference.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: A cool down is a period of light exercise after strenuous activity that allows the body to gradually return to its resting state. It helps remove waste products and speeds up recovery.

steps.title: EPOC (Excess Post-exercise Oxygen Consumption)
steps.body: The elevated oxygen intake after exercise that helps repay the oxygen debt and supports the breakdown of lactic acid. An active cool down supports EPOC more effectively than complete rest.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always name all four phases of the warm up in order - examiners look for this specific sequence Remember: warm up = dynamic stretching, cool down = static stretching When explaining benefits, link the physical change to the performance outcome (e.g. "increased temperature → more pliable muscles → reduced injury risk") Use the term "lactic acid removal" not "lactic acid removal through sweating" - it is removed via blood circulation to the liver Know the difference between EPOC and oxygen debt - they are related but distinct concepts When asked about cool down benefits, always mention preventing blood pooling and reducing DOMS
